brief: Cboe's weekly derivatives note reports cross-asset implied vol jumping last week, led by equities: the VIX gained over 16pts week-over-week to a 1-year high of 36%, but z-score comparisons show equity vol far outpacing other asset classes, meaning the move was driven more by equity positioning than broad macro de-risking. Bonds rallied on safety demand (MOVE Index to 106bps vol); credit spreads widened (VIXIG to 38bps, still below March highs); commodities fell broadly, gold down over 9% and oil near a 3-month low, while gold implied vol became the richest cross-asset vol (near 3 std dev above average). Friday's 7.4pt VIX jump was orderly: SPX's spot sell-off plus higher fixed-strike vol explained ~90% of it, with skew/convexity adding just 0.9pt, versus near half from downside-protection demand on Nov 5th. Falling call skew and unchanged call convexity signal no rebound positioning. Single-stock vol hit a 1-year high, outpacing index vol, as dispersion rose on rotation out of AI into other sectors rather than indiscriminate selling. Tech vol led gains; small-cap vol lagged, narrowing the RTY-SPX spread to a 6-year low.
